name: Defense Health Agency
description: DoD's combat support agency for the Military Health System. Buys MHS GENESIS, PEO DHMS, OPMED (operational medicine systems including JOMIS and MHS GENESIS-Theater), EIDS, HCDS, enterprise imaging, and the cyber and data modernization layer beneath them. Reorganized April 20, 2026 with FOC target July 19; Office of Warfighter Health Advantage (OWHA) consolidates data, analytics, AI, and digital health.
mmtRead: DHA reorganized April 20, 2026 with FOC target July 19. PEO DHMS retains executive authority over MHS GENESIS, OPMED programs (JOMIS, MHS GENESIS-Theater, deployable / Role 1-2-3 medical C2, blood inventory, theater data movement), and DMIX / EIDS. Organizationally PEO DHMS sits under AD-RDA/CAE, but the EHR portfolio's acquisition reporting runs directly to USW(A&S). The Office of Warfighter Health Advantage (RDML Tracy Farrill, just appointed) consolidates data, analytics, AI, and digital health into a single seat. The HCDS deployment RFP and the Leidos bridge are both inside the three-PAE transition window. Per the June 9, 2026 AD-RDA All Hands, the formal portfolios are PAE Medical Systems (MS), Medical Products (MP), and Medical Digital Solutions (MDS); PAE MDS is the consolidation seat absorbing PEO DHMS and PEO Medical Systems.

dataStrategy.title: FY2026-2030 Data Strategy
dataStrategy.summary: DHA frames data as a trusted, mission-enabling strategic asset across combat support, healthcare delivery, and operational efficiency. Five lines of effort define the operating model. Source-backed vendor implications below.

lines_of_effort.name: Data Roles and Responsibilities
lines_of_effort.vendor_implication: Governance, RACI documentation, data-steward enablement, training pipelines, role-based access design.

lines_of_effort.name: Authoritative Data Sources (ADS)
lines_of_effort.vendor_implication: ADS designation services, source-of-truth analytics, deduplication, system-of-record consolidation.

lines_of_effort.name: Operationalizing Data as a Product
lines_of_effort.vendor_implication: Product-oriented data engineering, consumer-grade interfaces, SLAs, lifecycle ownership, internal data-product teams.

lines_of_effort.name: Data Quality and Transparency
lines_of_effort.vendor_implication: Enterprise data quality scorecards, automated lineage, observability tooling, public-facing quality dashboards.

lines_of_effort.name: Enterprise Data Catalog (EDC)
lines_of_effort.vendor_implication: Catalog metadata governance, ADS registration workflows, integration with EDC, search and discovery layers.

name: Department of Health and Human Services
type: Cabinet Department (parent of CMS, NIH, FDA, CDC, IHS, ONC, ARPA-H)
description: HHS just realigned. As of January 2026, OMAS (the Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions) is the new contracting activity for all common IT, professional services, and what used to flow through ACF and AHRQ. The department dropped from 13 contracting activities to 10. If you sell common IT or advisory services into HHS, your contracting officer moved. If you sell mission-unique work to NIH, CDC, CMS, FDA, HRSA, IHS, ASPR, ARPA-H, or OIG, you stay where you are.
mmtRead: HHS is two stories now, not one. The mission-unique side (NIH for research IT, CMS for claims, FDA for surveillance, ARPA-H for OTA-funded R&D) still buys at the operating division. The common side (laptops, cloud, cybersecurity tools, advisory services, training) flows through OMAS strategic buying centers under EO 14240 and OMB M-25-31. Your BD calendar needs both maps: the operating-division map for mission, the OMAS SBC map for common. Expect the picture to keep moving — the FY26 Budget in Brief signals 28 operating divisions consolidating to 15 plus 5 regional offices closing.

policyModule.title: EO 14240 + OMB M-25-31 + PACT
confirmed_facts: EO 14240 (Procurement Consolidation, March 20, 2025) mandates transfer of common goods/services procurement to GSA — the root authority behind PACT.
OMB M-25-31 (Consolidating Federal Procurement Activities, July 18, 2025) is the implementation guidance: increased GSA use + procurement function centralization at GSA.
PACT (Procurement Alignment and Collaboration Task Force) is now an HHS Agency Priority Goal.
OMAS was realigned under ASFR/Office of Acquisitions in January 2026; staffing grew from ~40 at standup to ~180 by May 2026.
ACF and AHRQ independent contracting authority was eliminated and absorbed by OMAS SBC-Mission.
vendor_watch: Vehicle posture: be on GSA MAS IT, NASA SEWP, NITAAC CIO-SP, OASIS+. These are the canonical buying paths OMAS leverages.

policyModule.title: CMS Health Technology Ecosystem
confirmed_facts: CMS describes the Health Technology Ecosystem as a collaborative vision to modernize the national digital health ecosystem, empower Medicare beneficiaries, improve outcomes, reduce provider burden, and drive value.
The official page highlights voluntary alignment of data networks, EHR systems, health app developers, providers, and innovators around a shared framework for data and access.

The page references expansion of CMS data-sharing capabilities, modern identity on Medicare.gov, launch of public infrastructure for provider data, and an RFI regarding digital health products for Medicare beneficiaries and interoperability infrastructure.

RFI engagement: position now on digital health products + interoperability infrastructure to influence framing.

policyModule.title: Data Modernization Action Plan (DMAP)
confirmed_facts: DMAP is FDA's data modernization framework anchored on three components: data drivers (high-value driver projects), repeatable data practices, and people/external partnerships.
DMAP positions data modernization as a regulatory mission enabler, supporting FDA's product-area centers, review activities, and post-market surveillance.
The published DMAP is a high-level strategy document; current FDA implementation status is communicated through individual center activity and follow-on publications.
vendor_watch: Repeatable data practices: shared services, common data models, reusable pipelines across centers.
Talent and external partnerships: workforce enablement, academic collaboration, public-private partnership posture.
Regulatory mission alignment: tooling that supports review, post-market surveillance, and inspection workflows.
Currentness caveat: DMAP framing should be paired with newer FDA implementation sources before publishing capture briefs to clients.

Capture posture is to align with the three DMAP components (drivers, practices, partnerships) and then trace into the specific center that owns the high-value driver project. Treat DMAP as stable framing, not a current acquisition forecast.

groups.note: OASIS+ comprises six contract families covering different size and socioeconomic categories. Each family has its own award pool and ordering rules.
OASIS+ covers professional services domains, structured to scope task orders into a category.

Task orders are issued by federal agencies through a Delegation of Procurement Authority (DPA) workflow with required training. The Symphony portal handles ordering activity. GSA publishes a contractor list updated weekly.

contractorRead: OASIS+ is the governmentwide IDIQ family for professional services. It is emphatically NOT a health IT-specific vehicle. The six contract families plus seven domains shape where task orders land. Capture posture for health IT vendors: position OASIS+ as the channel for advisory, management, R&D, or enterprise-solutions work adjacent to health IT delivery (program management, capture strategy, evaluation studies). Do not market OASIS+ as a direct health IT acquisition lane; that mischaracterization will fail evaluator scrutiny.
